XJ01: Strong repeated positive signal: light, easy to pick up/use; electric alternatives described as heavy.
JD: Repeated platform-visible signal: light / not tiring; solidity also appears.
Failure Lexicon: Heaviness = canonical failure; Lightness × Credibility is a governing tension.
Amazon Reviewed: Mop: direct heaviness failure; squeegee: direct heaviness; bucket: imbalance/heaviness + positive lightness in value rows.
Design Implication: Protect visual/physical low burden, but test credibility separately; do not equate lighter colour with better.

XJ01: Strong: clean floor, absorbency, low residual water/watermarks.
JD: Strong: absorbency, less residual water, easy rinse.
Failure Lexicon: Maintenance/Hygiene gates; streak is not canonical but directly relevant.
Amazon Reviewed: Squeegee shows direct poor water removal/streak failures and positive no-streak counter-evidence; mop/brush show task-effectiveness failures.
Design Implication: Add water-removal/streak and task-effectiveness as product-specific validation gates; CMF cannot substitute for cleaning performance.

XJ01: Strong: installation, push-pull wringing, head change, low-contact operation.
JD: Ease of use and grip appear.
Amazon Reviewed: Mop: opening/wringing force, sticking mechanism, instruction/affordance failures. Bucket: pedal intermittency, collapse difficulty, assembly failures.
Design Implication: Signal/texture grammar must be validated at actual mechanism nodes; add force, assembly and discoverability tasks.

XJ01: Strong product-specific value: PU remains soft and avoids hardening.
Amazon Reviewed: Cleaning brushes show the opposite risk: bristles that are too soft reduce cleaning effectiveness.
Design Implication: Do not universalize 'soft = good'. Contact-zone material semantics must be task-specific: PU softness good for sponge mop; brush stiffness must retain scrubbing efficacy.

JD: Compactness appears with a coverage trade-off.
Failure Lexicon: Soil/maintenance and storage context are relevant; Storage Bulk not canonical.
Amazon Reviewed: Bucket shows collapse effort and size/context fit; squeegee compact storage positive; brush off-floor storage positive.
Design Implication: Validate storage volume together with deployment effort and cleaning coverage; compactness is not a standalone win.

XJ01: Perceived quality and durability language exists; some durability claims are user inference.
JD: Sturdy/solid language plus short-term damage counterexamples.
Failure Lexicon: Rust, Breakage, Looseness, Burr are canonical or tracked risks.
Amazon Reviewed: Direct bucket rust/breakage/leakage, squeegee breakage/looseness, mop/brush flimsiness and interface failures.
Design Implication: Appearance–Performance Coherence becomes a hard gate; premium finish cannot compensate for weak joints, corrosion or cheapness perception.

XJ01: Appearance is explicitly valued; exact hue preference unknown.
JD: Appearance/colour-positive language appears; no controlled hue preference.
Amazon Reviewed: Brush/squeegee rows directly show appearance attraction and bathroom-fixture integration, including cases where attractive products were judged functionally weak/cheap.
Design Implication: Appearance is legitimate value, but specific hue/finish remains unvalidated. Context integration and credibility should be separate perceptual axes.

XJ01: Easy cleaning/rinsing and wet-zone use repeat.
Failure Lexicon: Soil Retention, Odour, Yellowing, Dirt Visibility retained as hygiene/ageing gates.
Amazon Reviewed: Brush shows off-floor storage/easy-clean benefits; bucket/mop evidence reinforces wet-system mechanism and corrosion risks.
Design Implication: Test real rinse recovery, drainage, wet storage and surface cleanliness rather than 'clean-looking' colour alone.

XJ01: No strong direct failure evidence in selected sample.
JD: Not a dominant current Baojiajie signal.
Amazon Reviewed: Direct bucket sealing/leakage failures; positive no-leak counter-evidence also appears.
Design Implication: Promote Leakage/Sealing to External Candidate; validate bucket/wet-system joints before canonical promotion.

XJ01: Long-handle/low-burden context exists; detailed dimensional preference not established.
JD: Compactness vs coverage and grip/solid handle appear.
Failure Lexicon: Not a single canonical failure term.
Amazon Reviewed: Brush: too short/small; squeegee: handle too small/short; bucket: capacity/context fit; positive reach/fit also appears.
Design Implication: Add product-topology-specific scale/reach/grip checks; avoid using CMF to visually miniaturize a product already near coverage limits.
